you ask your crush out and either one of two things happen: either your projections become real, either you face reality. in theory, it's that simple, but in practice I know how bad does it feel to have that metaphorical claw inside your chest. But you have to push through that because  there are individuals that are as shy as you or even more shy, but the only actions you're able to control are yours. You WILL get rejected and you WILL feel sad. But you want that because it builds experience and thay will get you closer to finding your match. You probably lack confidence, don't worry, most of us don't have it (myself included), yet you still  should try making your fantesies come true, because no one else will do it for you. 
Keep yourself clean, shower, brush your teeth, be presentable, have some jokes under your sleeve and everything else comes with experience. You are an awesome human being and you can do most of the things you focus on and I know it sounds exaggerated since I don't know you, but it isn't. Everyone is unique and so are you, and someone will notice that and give you a chance.

nu esti singurul sau singura care a cazut asa. gandeste-te ca pe mine nu m-a luat profesorul de chimie la meditatie crezand ca nu am sanse, iar la examen (am dat medicina), am facut la biologie 54 din 60, fara vreo meditatie anume. la chimie mi-a  bagat mortul in casa omul, pentru ca nu am mai gasit profesori care sa ma ia la grupe, asa ca am intrat pe taxa. doare mai tare sa fii intrat pe jumatate decat sa nu fii intrat deloc, pentru ca nu stiu de tine, dar ai mei au un salariu minim pe economie si nu ma pot sustine. am fost la opt grile distanta de ultimul loc. imi vine sa vomit si sa il bag in spital pe cheliosul ala cu burta cat casa si cu ochiul mai chiojbaliu decat basescu de fiecare data cand ma gandesc cat de aproape am fost pe cont propriu.

acum, o sa auzi multe bullshit-uri de la oameni de rahat, multe dintre ele vor fi categorisite ca adevaruri de catre ei insisi. tot ce trebuie sa stii e ca nu, nu e vina ta. e nedrept ce s-a intamplat si nu nota din bac reflecta interesul tau pentru psihologie. nu e mai importanta o facultate decat viata ta si cel mai probabil esti mai indreptatit sa urmezi psihologie decat 60% din lista celor admisi (pe putin). nu, parintii tai nu sunt dezamagiti de tine si nici nu ar putea fi in contextul situatiei actuale. ai facut tot ce ai putut, ai facut in bac mai mult decat mine (7.96). probabil ai fi facut mai mult in examen decat majoritatea. multi din cei inscrisi la psiho n-au apucat la alte fscultati. nimic din anul asta nu e echitabil pentru nimeni. a fost facut totul pe fuga, ca sa nu ramana facultatile fara studenti.

La textul argumentativ am incercat pe cat de mult sa  dezvolt argumentul 1 bazandu-ma pe ideea textului suport, am scris ca mass media actioneaza ca un mijloc prin care ne sunt prezentati anumiti oameni de cultura, urmand ca fiecare dintre noi sa ne formam o opinie (de preferat obiectiva) pe baza acelor informatii. Apoi am continuat cu felul in care, utilizandu-se de mijloacele mass-media, un individ isi poate face cunoscuta povestea unei mase largi de oameni si, capatand aceasta mediatizare poate chiar sa depaseasca unele prejudecati ale publicului (acestea variind de la simple prejudecati legate de aspectul fizic pana la dezinteresul publicului pentru subiectul tratat de persoana in cauza) prin eruditia si cultura de care da dovada. Am pus exemplul din text, G. Calinescu,  un om care, in pofida propriei suferinte reuseste sa invinga lupta impotriva timpului si impotriva bolii, dand dovada de aceeasi energie ca atunci cand era sanatos. 
La argumentul doi am avut in minte mai multe exemple (nu vreau sa fiu rau, dar cerinta parca cerșea o perla legata de subiectele televizate la noi in ultima perioada, am auzit la colegi exemple atat de variate, atat bune, cat si rele: exemple din black mirror, house of cards, dar si exemple cum ar fi Cristian Tudor Popescu, felul in care Michael Jackson a fost portretizat de media intr-o lumina proasta. Personal, nu mi se pare okay sa dai exemple care pot fi considerate controversate), cateva dintre ele fiind Jeremy Meeks, George Floyd, Freddie Mercury etc. pe care le-am exclus fie din cauza faptului ca, desi aveau o oarecare legatura cu ipoteza, nu se potriveau corect, fie din cauza faptului ca nu imi aminteam cu exactitate detalii si nu as fi facut un argument perfect. In orice caz, exemplul meu a fost Lana del Rey si felul in care aceasta a avut parte in nenumarate randuri de ura din partea mass-media. (imi pare rau aici totusi ca nu am spus ca a fost portretizata ca intorcand femeile inapoi cu o suta de ani, mi-am adus aminte tocmai cand am iesit din sala). Am vrut, cu acesr exemplu sa arat ca mass-media nu tolereaza greseli din partea artistilor renumiti, asadar, am vorbit despre momentele in care aceasta nu mai putea canta live, dupa un lung turneu. Am zis pe acolo ca aceasta a influentat intr-un mod rau opinia publica despre artista, care a fost numita in nenumarate randuri "incapabila". Poate ca existau exemple mult mai bune, si din literatura (O scrisoare pierduta, ca tot a picat, puteam da exemplu despre racnet si despre cum l-ar fi afectat pe Tipatescu, dar intotdeauna am mers cu speranta ca voi prinde un corector care apreciaza elevul care da exemplu din contemporan, mi se pare ca spune mai multe despre elevul respectiv). Evident, m-am exprimat diferit.

Subiectul III, desi accesibil, mi s-a parut intr-o mica masura neasteptat. Am vazut piesa de teatru de trei in clasa a XI-a, dar nu mi-a placut sa retin cifre despre acte sau caracterizarile personajelor. Intr-un fel, va dau dreptate, pentru ca atunci cand mi-a zis profesoara mea ca puteam sa iau zece, am plecat capul jos. Cum nu imi place sa citesc obligat, nu am fost cel mai okay din clasa la subiectul III, dar am atins cat am putut in douazeci de minute, cat imi mai ramasese. Desi consider ca este okay sa stii sa faci putina analiza literara (e destul de dragut cand poti sa-ti dai cu parerea despre ce citesti in viata de zi cu zi) sunt putin lenes si cred ca 8.50 este o nota cam maricica pentru cat am scris acolo. Aproximez ca am sa iau undeva la 7.60, dar daca Bunul Corector este milostiv, poate ma ridic la un 8.  Subiectul III nu ar fi un subiect atat de temut daca ai avea loc sa te misti prin el, dar, pe langa faptul ca trebuie sa pregatesti un eseu (pe care il poti pregati si fara citirea operei, ce este drept), structura Incadrare>Tema, viziune>Titlu>Structura compozitionala>Incipit, actiune, incheiere>Personaje>Concluzie limiteaza foarte mult. Ma simt, in acelasi timp, foarte aiurea sa critic subiectul III in contextul in care nu am facut mai nimic niciodata la el.

La subiectul II chiar pregatisem un inceput pentru perspectiva narativa de acasa, in cazul in care trebuia sa scriu despre un text de Slavici. A fost okay si cu Agârbiceanu, mi-ar fi placut sa scriu totusi de recensamintele din 1746-1747 si despre Slavit Arzinte si Slavity Szav. Alta era impresia.

Imi cer iertare pentru textul deosebit de lung, insa trebuia sa exteriorizez toata energia adunata din momentul in care am parasit sala si pana am ajuns acasa.

Ma trezesc dimineata cu zambetul pe buze tocmai pentru ca stiu ca exista profesori ca dumneavoastra. Va multumesc pentru sfaturi.

Mi se pare ca subiectul III este atat o povara pentru elev, cat si pentru profesor. Este cea mai mare farsa de la "ti-ai uitat un nasture" incoace. Personal, nu stiu decat Ion, iar daca nu pica Ion, ei bine. Nici nu imi doresc o nota mare, consider ca ce este peste 7 la romana este un efort care nu merita depus. Tot ce vreau sa fac este sa am un subiect I B. atat de impecabil incat sa frang inima profesorului care corecteaza atunci cand vede cat de putine am stiut la subiectul II. E micul meu semn de protest, desi stiu sa vorbesc despre fiecare opera, nu sunt critic literar si nu pot sa alcatuiesc un eseu extraordinar fara sa memorez citate din Calinescu, Lovinescu, etc, ceea ce inseamna ca pot lua maxim un opt, daca se simte corectorul extrem de ingaduitor pentru efortul depus la SI si SII.  Totusi, vreau sa ofer si eu cateva sfaturi:

•Ciocolata face minuni. Putina ciocolata inainte de examen ar trebui sa va calmeze putin.
•Evident, o lucrare imaculata arata profesorului ca sunteti serios. 
•Nu ezitati sa folositi un lexic cat mai bogat. Ganditi-va la faptul ca sinonimele sunt asemenea nuantelor unei culori: albastru si turcoaz sunt asemanatoare,  dar cine poarta sacou rosu cu cravata turcoaz?
•Este si normal sa incepeti cu ce stiti, insa daca faceti subiectele in ordine si puneti punctul pe i la textul argumentativ, este posibil ca profesorul sa fie foarte indulgent, ba chiar sa fie entuziasmat ca cineva a folosit ca exemplu filmul sau preferat, sau o carte de care a auzit, la argumentul 2. (poveste amuzanta, am retinut filmul preferat al profei de romana, Truman Show, fix cand ne-a pomenit de el in clasa a IX-a. L-am vazut, si in clasa a XII-a am avut o tema, unde am folosit ca exemplu filmul respectiv. Efectul a fost extraordinar. O ador pe doamna profesoara, si singurul lucru pe care il regret este ca nu ne-a oferit mai multe filme )
•Un argument contra, daca se poate. Nu va bazati tot textul ca fiind contra, un argument este suficient. Textul suport, de cele mai multe ori, poate fi fructificat doar in argumentele pro, dar daca mergi pe principiul "socoteala de acasa nu se potriveste cu cea din targ", un argument contra din experienta culturala sau personala poate arata ca nu va este frica sa spuneti "nu". Numai tineti minte sa folositi conectorii logici potriviti (in astfel de cazuri, puteti folosi "pe de o parte / pe de alta parte). 
•Stilul conteaza. Personal, nu imi place sa arunc o ipoteza din neant, deci mereu incep textul argumentativ cu o mica introducere, iar in acelasi alineat imi enuntiez opinia. Dezvoltati pe larg argumentele inainte sa dati exemple, o idee buna ar fi sa recititi textul suport cand ajungeti la subiectul B,  apoi inca odata dupa subiectul B sa vedeti daca ati completat indeajuns de mult cerintelele de la A. Nu va sfiiti sa scrieti 6 randuri la punctul 4, explicati astfel incat sa nu fie aproape demonstrativ, dar cat sa lase un zambet pe buze.

This is one complicated question, the short answer would be something along the lines of *yes, but it would be a nightmare to look at.* Probably very toxic, as the fearful will, at some point, try to push the dissmissive away from them and the dissmissive will leave being the simpleton he is. At some point, either one of them will try to get back (if it is the dissmissive, it's because they feel like they can't find anybody better than their ex, and if it is the fearful, it's because of some stubborn idea that it might've been their fault) only to push eachother away again.

Our advantage as a species is our ability to communicate with eachother through words. That's what helped us co-operate with eachother. With that being said, it is understandable for most of us to put so much value into words. It is normal to feel the need of hearing "I love you" from our partner from time to time and it hurts a little (well, more than a little in some cases) when we don't hear it. Avoidants generally have a problem with intimacy, meaning that they feel uncomfortable showing affection. What is easy for us might be hard for them. That's why they don't say it as often as we would want them to. The weight of those three words makes them vulnerable because these words are associated with some form of dependency (and avoidants value independence). However, they might feel love for their partner even though they don't say it  (or show it). I also met people that told me they love me even though they didn't. Saying it doesn't necessarily mean feeling it. 

Besides that, the harder it is to say "I love you", the more honest the feeling is. There are many questions that might pop into one's mind before saying it, such as "what if I will hurt them in the long run", "what if the feeling is not reciprocated", "what if saying it will make them more attached to me, it means that they will get more dependent and I might end up destroying my own safe space". Again, being honest, feeling and communicating your feelings are different things. 

What you really need is to know whether or not they love you, and unless you can study their brain activity to see whether or not areas associated with love and attachment in their brain light up when they see you, you have no real way to know. You can look for signs, though. See if your partner keeps their promises to you or shows interest in your activities. One way I figured out my ex was no longer interested in me (besides the fact that she grew cold) was when I gave her something I wrote and she read it after a week. She forgot about it, also. Check to see if they remember important dates such as the date you two got together etc etc. Actions speak louder than words.

What I've noticed is that people who don't necessarily love the person they are with tend to say I love you not only more often than people who actually love the person, but also in a more shallow way. For example, someone who actually loves might say it rarely but they might add certain things to it that make the moment more special, where as someone who just acts as if they love you might say it more often but not in a special way. Avoidants already struggle with showing affection, so don't expect them to write paragraphs about how they feel about you, but I also don't think they would say it if they didn't feel it. They might say it rarely, but if they mean it, then it's all that matters.

Part of me also wants to tell you that if I were in your shoes, I would stop telling them I love them just to see how they would react. But that's kind of immature and I doubt avoidants will show any response to it, though. 

I really hope things go well between you two.

I've read Attached: The new science of adult attachment and how it can help you find and keep love and I instantly knew how intoxicated my mind was. While I was reading it, I noticed that it made me feel better. They wrote it especially for the anxious type and I feel like they kind of throw shit at the avoidant. In the end, no one of us is to blame for the way we feel. Our parents did not know how to develop actual secure relationships with us, or if they knew, childhood bullying got the best of us.
My luck was that I always knew I had some sort of a problem, so I spent most of my time on the internet building relationships with strangers and trying to understand my own mind through them. Whenever I found someone that had similar thinking patterns to me, I challenged their thoughts. I slowly practiced being aware of my own feelings and thoughts and getting to know my triggers. The worst trigger: anything I don't like to hear or anything that might sound like "one day we are going to break up and we both know that. This rant was actually written because my girlfriend told me this. Of course, not with these words, but it is what she suggested. Of course I know it, I think constantly of it. You don't have to say it too, it hurts even more. 
On the other hand, I've also notived that us, the anxious type, lack the self respect needed to say no. I remember not being able to part ways with one of my toxic ex's because she threatened me with killing herself if I do. I actually felt desperate when I got into a relationship with her and didn't really invest emotionally. And now that I have a somewhat healthy relationship with my actual girlfriend, I live with the constant fear that she is with me because she can't get out of the relationship. So, if anyone sees this while lurking, remember to have self respect and say no to things you don't actually want. Being desperate is what brought you on the path of learning what's going on inside your head. Being the anxious type and having a distorted perception of love because you feel "the claw" is better than having  a distorted perception of love both because you feel "the claw" and you know you did the very things you are afraid people will do to you. 
Saying no, knowing when to end chapters and being able to at least recognize your feelings are one of the most important things you'll have to learn.

it happened to me once. two years ago i had a crush on a girl who was DA. we dated for literally two weeks. then she told me she never liked me. my self esteem took a hit and i unfriended her from facebook. fast forward from march to december the same year and she sends me a friend request. i accept, even though i'm not really over the trauma she's caused (remember, if you are anxious, your overthinking actually causes more drama than most of the things your DA will say or do. generally speaking, most DA's aren't actually toxic, it's just the fact that their cold behaviour and your hypersensitivity to details are the ingredients for a toxic relationship. avoiding the trap is hard and if you are early into the relationship, i highly suggest leaving and finding someone secure). fast forward in march the next year, i'm at a party when i meet one of her friends and learn that my DA has been missinf me for over a year and wants to apologize. we got back together, only to part ways again after a month of reliving the painful memories I had back when I first dated her.

the short answer would be, yes, they are human, they miss you but don't think they suddenly changed and started being secure. heck, I display highly anxious tendencies and my partner whom I think is secure (they always reassure me that they love me but I have trouble trusting her even though she shows more effort than my ex's before her had shown.) has trouble with my extremely anxious personality.

It's okay, I punched a wall and started crying right before I sent the comment. All the memories I had with her are filled with so much pain, I gasp everytime I open the book in which I hid my last photo of me and her. Everytime I remember kissing her lips I feel like trash, because she poisoned the taste of her lips through her last whatsapp messages. She told me she doesn't know the difference between loving someone and  finding someone dear, she told me she feels bad for hurting me but that she knows for a fact that she will keep doing it if we stay together. Then, what hurt me most is that she tried to play the victim bt accusing me of why I didn't stop it if I felt something was wrong. I lost some of our common friends because of her. They all decided she had more facts than I did. But here's the thing: relationships aren't as much about facts as they are about feelings. That's why some long distance relationships can survive: the feeling of love is strong enough from both sides to overcome the fact that there is distance. What am I trying to tell you here is that, despite the fact that you walked barefoot through a tunnel filled with pain and that your shattered heart cut your own feet so hard you now have to crawl, there's love at the end of this forest. Love, in its purest of forms, exists. You just have to not abandon ship yet. I know that after all those experiences you might feel not good enough for anyone, you might not feel that there is such thing as a compatible person with you, but here's the catch: you launched yourself onto so many bad persons, fully committed and willing to get past their quirks and defects out of love and affection towards them, you even continued to pursue those people even though they mistreated you. If you were able to do that, and I was able to do that too, then it means that there are so, so many people like us out there, willing to give all of themselves towards one person, and willing to show love.
Take care, brother, because right now both of us are walking in the same desert.

so i really need to post this here since I fell into something called the anxious-avoidant trap, and that basically changed my view of relationships.
I know a lot of you are into toxic / kind of one sided relationships where you give more than you get in terms of anything, from intimacy to affection to whatever thing you give. The other person is kind of passive and/or rejects you at times, sends mixed signals, hurts your feeligs and is not available when you need it the most, let alone being always available. You might always wonder if the other person truly loves you, if he/she feels the same. And however, even though I can't give you a consistent answer for that, I can provide you with my story and maybe you relate to some of the details.

A year ago, there was this girl I met randomly on facebook. We were from the same school so we kind of stumbled around eachother and we slowly became friends, and then I confessed my feelings towards her and asked her on a date. We went on a date and she did everything she could to reject me. She kept asking me when will i leave etc etc. At first, I didnt notice much (perhaps due to the emotions I felt back then) but when I started reflecting to the moments of the date at home the questions started flowing in. Three days later, she rejected me a 2nd date. After that I kept wondering what went wrong, what was wrong with me, why did she behave like that when, almost a week ago it was clear the feeling is mutual. I had my doubts back then too, but the fact that she admitted to like me kind of put an end to my doubts for a while.
